source.title: Parameter Reduction Improves Vision Transformers: A Comparative Study of Sharing and Width Reduction

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling laws as background but does not test any listed version: its experiments compare parameter-reduced ViT-B/16 classifiers on ImageNet-1K, rather than measuring language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy for a ViT-B/16 baseline and two parameter-reduced variants. These classification results do not measure the loss scaling or other behaviors named by the claim versions. References to scaling laws are background context, not tested results.
record.test_reason: Scaling laws appear only as background motivation. The experiments compare three ViT-B/16 classifiers at one scale (86.6M vs 58.2M parameters) on ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy. There is no loss-versus-scale curve, no power-law fit, no compute-optimal allocation, and no language-model pretraining loss. The fewer-parameters-beats-baseline result is a single-point comparison in vision classification. It does not test V5's power-law form or V1's loss scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that, for ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K under their recipe, MLP parameter sharing or width reduction slightly improves accuracy and substantially improves training stability. They read this as overparameterization, with the reduced capacity acting as an inductive bias.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains modified vision classifiers and reports ImageNet classification outcomes; it does not apply the language-model loss-scaling or compute-allocation method.

fits_no_version.finding: Two ViT-B/16 variants with 32.7% fewer MLP parameters slightly beat the 86.6M baseline on top-1 accuracy (81.47% and 81.25% vs 81.05%). They also cut the peak-to-final degradation from 0.47% to 0.03–0.06%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K under a standard 300-epoch recipe, reducing MLP capacity by sharing or halving width does not hurt accuracy and slightly improves it.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched 58.2M parameters, sharing MLPs (GroupedMLP) and halving MLP width (ShallowMLP) differ by only 0.22 points of top-1 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ViT-B/16 image classification, how MLP parameters are arranged at fixed parameter count changes accuracy only slightly. This is a vision-accuracy analogue of V4, not a test of it.

record.problems: The study is limited to one model size, one dataset, one training recipe, two parameter-reduction designs, and two random seeds. It does not measure the claim's loss-scaling relationships.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported outcomes, including top-5 accuracy, peak-to-final accuracy gap, throughput, memory, and FLOPs, do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss and no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted law and no extrapolation.
No compute-budget sweep or optimal parameter/token allocation.
There is a matched-parameter comparison of two shapes (shared vs narrower MLP). It is ViT classification accuracy at one size, not LM pretraining loss across a shape range.
Vision models are used, but only one model size is trained, so no power-law form can be assessed.
No relation between scale or pretraining loss and downstream performance is measured.
No exponent fitting and no comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Only one model scale, two seeds and one dataset are used. The baseline's late-training degradation (accuracy falls, loss rises after about epoch 220) suggests overfitting under this recipe. Such overfitting is outside the 'other factors not the bottleneck' regime that V1 assumes, so the result is not evidence against the scaling laws.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses vision models but does not test whether a power-law form holds in vision or another training regime.

rows.subject: Baseline
rows.operation_detail: Train the ViT-B/16 baseline on ImageNet-1K.
rows.note: Reported as the reference model for the parameter-reduced variants; classification accuracy does not measure a claim version.

rows.subject: GroupedMLP
rows.operation_detail: Share MLP weights between adjacent transformer blocks, then train.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± std over two seeds; p=0.018 versus baseline
rows.note: The result is for image classification accuracy, not a power-law measurement of held-out loss.

rows.subject: ShallowMLP
rows.operation_detail: Reduce the MLP hidden dimension from 3072 to 1536 across blocks, then train.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± std over two seeds; p=0.031 versus baseline
rows.note: The result is for image classification accuracy, not a power-law measurement of held-out loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
